# ATST Playground

> Tools for learning how to create and verify ENS text record attestations.

An ATST attestation is a signed claim that the owner of an ENS name also
controls a particular social media account. The envelope holds only a version,
a timestamp and a signature; every other field is reconstructed by the verifier
from ENS at verification time, so any change to the underlying records breaks
signature recovery. The playground makes each of those steps visible.

## Pages

- [Attest](/): Build a payload, sign it with a throwaway key, and get back the
  envelope and the text record key it belongs under.
- [Verify](/): Walk a live mainnet name through Section 7 of the spec one step
  at a time, showing the resolved owner, the handle record, the decoded
  envelope, the reconstructed payload, its digest, and the recovered signer.
- [Inspect](/): Decode an envelope and edit any reconstructed field to see
  recovery diverge, which is how the spec's failure modes present in practice.

## Specification

- [ATST format](https://atst.me/): The attestation format this app implements.
- [ENSIP-27](https://docs.ens.domains/ensip/27): The related ENS improvement
  proposal.

## API

- [POST /api/verify](/api/verify): Verify an on-chain attestation and return the
  full step-by-step trace as JSON. Body: `name`, `platform`, `attester`, `mode`
  (`handle` or `uid`), and `uid` when mode is `uid`. See
  [/.well-known/agent-card.json](/.well-known/agent-card.json).

## Notes

The app reads Ethereum mainnet and never writes. Publishing an attestation means
setting the text record yourself.
